text: Shows a single Mac window or the whole Mac desktop on an iPhone or iPad, controlled with touch, keyboard or Apple Pencil
quote: Sill shows a window from your Mac, or its whole desktop, on your iPhone or iPad, and lets you use it with touch, a keyboard or Apple Pencil.

text: Taps, clicks, momentum scrolling, an on-screen trackpad, keys and typed text, with Apple Pencil acting as the pointer
quote: taps and clicks, scrolls with momentum, the on-screen trackpad, keys and typed text, and Apple Pencil as the pointer.

text: Three-finger swipes and pinches trigger Mac trackpad gestures such as Mission Control, App Exposé, Spaces and Show Desktop
quote: Three fingers swipe and pinch as on a Mac's trackpad: Mission Control, App Exposé, the Spaces, Apps and Show Desktop

text: A keyboard attached to the iPhone or iPad types on the Mac as soon as the picture shows, including Esc
quote: A keyboard attached to your device types on your Mac as soon as the picture shows, Esc included

text: Clipboard moves both ways: Mac copies can be pasted on the device, and Paste in Sill sends the device clipboard to the Mac
quote: text you copy on your Mac is ready to paste on your device, and Paste in Sill sends what you copied on your device to your Mac's clipboard

text: Menus of the active Mac app appear in the iPad menu bar on iPadOS 26 or later, and behind a Menus button in Sill's bar
quote: The menus of the app you use reach your device too: in the iPad's own menu bar on iPadOS 26 or later, and behind the Menus button in Sill's bar.

text: Launch any Mac app from a searchable Apps list that shows open apps and every installed app
quote: "Launch any Mac app." Sill's Apps list on an iPad held sideways, with a search field, the apps open now and every app installed on the Mac.

text: Window thumbnails in Sill's bar switch between Mac windows, and holding a thumbnail offers Close, Minimize and Full Screen
quote: "Every window, one tap away." On an iPad held sideways, a window's thumbnail held in Sill's bar shows Close, Minimize and Full Screen.

text: Aa resizes the streamed Mac window through Accessibility so its text shows at the size you pick
quote: Aa on your device resizes the window you stream on your Mac, through Accessibility, so its text shows at the size you pick

text: Optional virtual display moves a streamed window onto its own display on the Mac so it keeps updating when other windows cover it
quote: The virtual display (off by default) moves a window you stream onto a display of its own on your Mac, so it keeps updating when other windows cover it.

text: Laptop mode on an upright iPad puts the Mac picture on top with a row of keys and a trackpad below
quote: "Laptop mode." An iPad held upright, with the Mac's Clock app on top and Sill's bar, a row of keys and a trackpad below it.

text: Larger Picture setting enlarges the window picture into the space used by the thumbnails
quote: Larger Picture, in the settings panel, gives a window's picture the room of the window thumbnails, down to where the keyboard comes up

text: Foldable support: half open, the picture sits above the fold with a trackpad and keys below; closed, Sill runs on the cover display
quote: half open like a laptop, the picture is above the fold with a trackpad and keys below; closed, Sill runs on the cover display.

text: Shows the Mac pointer's position on the device when someone moves the mouse at the Mac
quote: When someone moves the mouse at your Mac, your device shows the pointer where it is.

text: Remote Access lets you use the Mac away from home through your own VPN, such as Tailscale, or a forwarded router port
quote: Remote Access lets you use your Mac away from home, through your own VPN, such as Tailscale, or through a port you forward on your router.

text: Away from home, sessions start at a quality a slower link can carry, then move to the home network automatically when you return
quote: Away from home, Sill starts at a quality a slower connection can carry, and when you get home, the session moves to your network by itself.

text: Direct Wireless Connection links a nearby iPhone or iPad to the Mac without a shared Wi-Fi network, like AirDrop
quote: Direct Wireless Connection lets an iPhone or iPad near your Mac connect without a shared Wi-Fi network, the way AirDrop does.

text: Pair by scanning a code shown on the Mac, or automatically over a USB cable
quote: it shows a code for your iPhone or iPad to scan, and over a USB cable the two pair by themselves.

text: Each device pairs with the Mac once, only paired devices can connect, and every connection is encrypted
quote: Each iPhone or iPad pairs with your Mac once. After that, only the devices you paired can connect, and every connection is encrypted.

text: Settings › Devices on the Mac lists paired devices and lets you remove ones you no longer use or have lost
quote: Sill's Settings › Devices on your Mac lists the devices you paired. Remove one you no longer use, or have lost.

text: Forget a paired Mac from the device's connect screen
quote: To forget one Mac you paired, touch and hold its row on the connect screen and choose Forget.

text: Pick a lower stream quality from the device settings panel or the Mac's Sill menu
quote: Pick a lower Quality in the settings panel on your iPhone or iPad, or in the Sill menu on your Mac.

text: The Mac detects when it is holding frames back, warns on the device, and offers a quality the link can carry
quote: Sill for Mac notices that it is holding frames back and tells your device, which says so over the picture and, in its Settings, offers a quality the link can carry.

text: No account and no server; screen and keystrokes travel only between your own devices
quote: There is no account and no server: your screen and what you type travel only between your own devices

text: Streams audio of what you view: the window's app, or every app when showing the desktop
quote: the sound of what you’re looking at: the window’s app, or every app for your desktop.

text: Pinch with two fingers to zoom the picture up to five times around the point between your fingers
quote: Pinch the picture with two fingers to zoom it, up to five times, around the point between your fingers.

text: Input method composition and candidate selection happen on the device, and the chosen text is typed on the Mac
quote: You compose and pick from the candidates on your device, and what you pick is typed on your Mac.

text: Reverse Scrolling setting on the device flips scroll direction
quote: To turn both around, turn on Reverse Scrolling under This iPad (This iPhone on iPhone) in the settings panel on your iPhone or iPad.

text: Launch at Login option makes Sill open on the Mac by itself
quote: To have Sill open by itself then, choose Launch at Login in the Sill menu, or turn it on in Sill’s Settings › General.

text: Option to show the pairing window to screen sharing so a remote viewer of the Mac can read the pairing code
quote: Turn on Show the pairing window to screen sharing in Sill’s Settings › Devices on your Mac; while it’s on, anyone who can see your Mac’s screen remotely can read the code.

text: Notifies you of new versions in its menu and Settings with a release link, but does not update itself
quote: Sill doesn't update itself, but it tells you when a new version is out: its menu and Settings say so, with a link to the release.

text: Daily update check against the GitHub API can be turned off in Settings › General
quote: Unless you turn off “Check for updates automatically” in Sill’s Settings › General, once a day it asks GitHub (api.github.com) whether a newer version of Sill has been released

text: Logs can be opened via Show Log… in the Sill menu or in Library/Logs
quote: On your Mac, choose Show Log… in the Sill menu, or open the Sill folder in Library/Logs in your home folder.

text: Install and upgrade via Homebrew cask from Sill's own tap
quote: brew install --cask saffsanity/sill/sill in Terminal installs the same Sill.dmg from Sill’s own tap. To update it, quit Sill and run brew upgrade --cask sill.

text: Verify the downloaded Sill.dmg against the SHA-256 published in GitHub release notes
quote: open Terminal, type shasum -a 256 and a space, drag Sill.dmg into the window and press Return. It should print the same SHA-256 as the release’s notes on GitHub

text: Nightly notarized Mac builds are published as a GitHub pre-release
quote: Nightly builds: every night the code changes, a notarized Sill for Mac built from it goes to the [nightly pre-release](https://github.com/Saffsanity/sill/releases/tag/nightly) on GitHub.

text: iPhone and iPad app available as a public TestFlight beta
quote: Sill for iPhone and iPad: join the [public beta on TestFlight](https://testflight.apple.com/join/6v7nqyn3).

text: Sill is free and open source
quote: Sill is free and open source.

text: Build script compiles Sill.app with SwiftPM, signs it with your Apple Development identity, and installs it into /Applications
quote: This builds Sill.app with SwiftPM, signs it with your Apple Development identity, replaces /Applications/Sill.app and opens it.

text: Run the host from the command line with swift run, including a synthetic test-pattern mode that needs no Screen Recording permission
quote: `swift run -c release SillHost` runs the same host on the command line... With `--synthetic` it streams a test pattern with no Screen Recording needed.
